subtitle: How a question of war became a charter of endurance

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Rajagriha's hill and fort, with Vassakara in foreground looking toward distant Vajji lands
panels.action: Vassakara of Magadha stands on a rocky outcrop near Rajagriha’s fort, his scholar-minister’s robes stirring in the wind, as hazy plains stretch away toward the unseen Vajji confederation beyond the hills.

dialogue.text: In Rajagriha, as Magadha eyed the Vajji confederation, a minister’s question drew from the Buddha seven habits said to keep a republic from decline.

i18n.hi: राजगृह में, जब मगध की नज़र वज्जि संघ पर थी, एक मंत्री के सवाल पर बुद्ध ने गणराज को संभाले रखने वाली सात आदतें गिनाईं।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Rajagriha’s city nestled among hills, early morning light
panels.action: The ancient city of Rajagriha lies between stone hills, its wooden palisades, gates, and clustered houses catching the pale light of dawn as smoke rises in thin columns from cooking fires.

dialogue.text: In the fifth century before the Common Era, the eastern plains were a patchwork of powers: monarchies like Magadha, and gana-sanghas like the Vajji confederation.

i18n.hi: ईसा से पाँचवीं सदी पहले, पूरा पूर्वी मैदान टुकड़ों में बँटा था: मगध जैसे राजतंत्र और वज्जि जैसे गण-संघ।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a simple royal office, Vassakara seated with palm-leaf documents, maps on a low table
panels.action: Vassakara of Magadha sits cross-legged beside a low table strewn with palm-leaf strips and a rough map of the Ganga valley, his face intent as he weighs the rival realms marked in ink.

dialogue.text: Magadha’s king Ajatashatru sought to expand his realm. To his minister Vassakara he entrusted a hard question: could the Vajji gana-sangha be broken?

i18n.hi: मगध का राजा अजातशत्रु अपना राज्य फैलाना चाहता था। उसने मंत्री वस्सकार को कठिन सवाल दिया: क्या वज्जि गण-संघ को तोड़ा जा सकता है?

panels.shot: slow push-in on Vassakara’s thoughtful face, interior dimly lit
panels.action: In the dim chamber, Vassakara’s eyes narrow in thought, a faint worry line between his brows, as distant sounds of the city fade beneath the weight of his charge.

dialogue.speaker: Vassakara of Magadha
dialogue.text: If they stand together, my king’s chariots may not be enough.

i18n.hi: अगर वे साथ रहे, तो महाराज के रथ भी कम पड़ सकते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Bamboo Grove monastery near Rajagriha, monks moving between trees, Vassakara at the edge
panels.action: At the edge of a quiet grove thick with bamboo, saffron-robed monks move in silence between simple huts as Vassakara stands at the entrance, hands folded, eyes scanning for the Teacher.

dialogue.text: The Pali sources remember a different move. Vassakara went not to a war council, but to the Buddha’s retreat near Rajagriha, seeking insight before steel.

i18n.hi: पाली ग्रंथ एक और चाल का ज़िक्र करते हैं। वस्सकार युद्ध-सभा नहीं, राजगृह के पास बुद्ध के विहार पहुँचा, लोहे से पहले समझ लेने।

panels.shot: medium shot of Vassakara seated respectfully before an unseen elder figure, focus on his posture and humility
panels.action: Vassakara kneels on a woven mat, back straight, hands joined in respect toward an unseen elder seated opposite, the air still save for a soft rustle of bamboo leaves.

dialogue.speaker: Vassakara of Magadha
dialogue.text: Can Magadha, lord, defeat the Vajji, if it should attack?

i18n.hi: भगवन्, क्या मगध वज्जि को हरा सकता है, अगर वे चढ़ आएँ?

panels.shot: close-up on Vassakara listening, face tilted, as if hearing a measured reply
panels.action: Vassakara’s face is turned slightly upward, attentive and cautious, as he listens to a calm voice that seems to weigh each word before offering it.

dialogue.text: The Mahaparinibbana Sutta does not give a direct yes or no. It preserves instead a teaching: first to a disciple, Ananda, and through him, to all who would hear.

i18n.hi: महापरिनिब्बान सुत्त सीधा हाँ या ना नहीं कहता। वह एक उपदेश रखता है: पहले आनंद को, और आनंद के ज़रिए, सब सुनने वालों को।

panels.shot: wide shot on a hillside near Rajagriha, the Buddha’s figure implied in silhouette, Ananda beside, Vassakara at a respectful distance
panels.action: On a gentle hillside above Rajagriha, an elder ascetic sits beneath a sparse tree, his calm profile in silhouette; Ananda sits close, attentive, while Vassakara stands a little apart, hands folded.

dialogue.text: The tradition places the scene on the eve of the Buddha’s last journey. Around him, disciples gathered; beyond, Magadha and Vajji watched one another in uneasy balance.

i18n.hi: परंपरा कहती है, ये दृश्य बुद्ध की अंतिम यात्रा से ज़रा पहले का है। चारों ओर शिष्य, दूर मगध और वज्जि, दोनों शक में, आँखें एक-दूजे पर।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on Ananda’s attentive face opposite the implied Buddha, Vassakara blurred in background
panels.action: Ananda’s calm yet earnest face fills the frame as he leans slightly forward to catch each phrase, while behind him Vassakara waits, a silent shadow beyond the inner circle.

dialogue.text: To Ananda, the Teacher is said to have spoken first of the Vajjis, not as enemies, but as a people held together by certain habits.

i18n.hi: आनंद से आचार्य ने पहले वज्जियों की बात की, दुश्मन नहीं, बल्कि आदतों से बँधा हुआ एक समाज कहकर।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the elder’s hand raised in gentle emphasis, Ananda’s hands folded, Vassakara listening
panels.action: An unseen elder’s hand is shown mid-gesture, fingers relaxed yet firm, as Ananda bows his head and Vassakara listens, eyes lowered out of deference.

dialogue.text: The texts list seven conditions for the Vajjis’ welfare: that they assemble often, meet in concord, honour their ancient customs, and obey their elders.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ वज्जियों के हित की सात शर्तें गिनते हैं: कि वे अक्सर जुटें, मेल से बैठें, पुरानी रीति मानें, और बड़ों की बात सुनें।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot of a Vajji assembly hall in Vaishali, elders seated in a circle, younger men standing respectfully around
panels.action: Inside a large wooden hall at Vaishali, rows of seated elders with topknots and simple ornaments face one another in a semicircle, while younger men stand behind them, hands crossed in respectful silence.

dialogue.text: The gana-sangha of Vajji was no open democracy. It was an assembly of clans and elders, yet its strength lay in gathering frequently and in ending debate without rancour.

i18n.hi: वज्जि का गण-संघ खुला जनतंत्र नहीं था। यह कुलों और बुज़ुर्गों की सभा थी, पर उसकी ताकत थी बार-बार जुटना और बहस बिना कड़वाहट के खत्म करना।

panels.shot: wide shot of the same hall, now showing elders greeting one another, a sense of continuity and ritual
panels.action: Vajji elders rise to greet one another with joined palms and slight bows, moving along a worn path in the hall, the beams darkened by years of smoke and use.

dialogue.text: The Pali canon remembers them as faithful to their old decisions, and as a body that respected its senior members, preserving continuity even as generations turned.

i18n.hi: पाली काणन याद रखता है कि वे अपने पुराने फैसलों पर टिके रहे, और बुज़ुर्गों को मान देते रहे, ताकि पीढ़ी बदले, पर धारा बनी रहे।

panels.shot: montage wide showing Vajji women walking safely in the streets of Vaishali, shrines and trees in the background
panels.action: In the streets of Vaishali, women walk with water pots and children at their side beneath flowering trees, passing simple shrines and stone markers without fear or hindrance.

dialogue.text: The seven conditions include this too: that women and young girls be protected, that shrines be cared for, and that ascetics be honoured and welcomed.

i18n.hi: सात शर्तों में ये भी है: कि स्त्रियाँ और कन्याएँ सुरक्षित रहें, देव-स्थलों की सेवा हो, और संन्यासियों को सम्मान और आसरा मिले।

panels.shot: medium shot of an ascetic being respectfully offered alms at a Vajji village gate, elders watching approvingly
panels.action: At a village gate under the Vajji domain, an emaciated wandering ascetic receives a bowl of food from a householder, while nearby elders watch with quiet approval.

dialogue.text: Anguttara Nikaya and Chinese parallels echo this picture. Care for religious sites and wandering renunciants was counted among the habits that kept the Vajjis united.

i18n.hi: अंगुत्तर निकाय और चीनी ग्रंथ भी यही तस्वीर दोहराते हैं। तीर्थों की देखभाल और घूमते त्यागियों का सत्कार, वज्जि की एकता की रोज़ की आदतें मानी गईं।

panels.shot: medium shot back in the grove, Ananda reciting the seven conditions aloud to Vassakara, the elder seated silently
panels.action: Back in the bamboo grove, Ananda sits facing Vassakara, calmly reciting, his fingers counting each condition, while the elder teacher sits behind, silent, eyes half-closed.

dialogue.text: According to the Mahaparinibbana Sutta, the Buddha bids Ananda recite these seven points in Vassakara’s hearing, as if to answer the minister without advising war.

i18n.hi: महापरिनिब्बान सुत्त के अनुसार, बुद्ध आनंद से कहते हैं कि ये सात बिंदु वस्सकार के सामने दुहराए, मानो मंत्री को बिना युद्ध की सलाह दिए जवाब हो।

panels.shot: close-up on Vassakara’s face, thoughtful and slightly troubled, as he processes the implications
panels.action: Vassakara’s face fills the frame, his gaze turned inward, lips pressed thin as he weighs the meaning of assemblies, concord, and protected customs for a plan of conquest.

dialogue.speaker: Vassakara of Magadha
dialogue.text: A people bound so, my king should not meet by chariot alone.

i18n.hi: ऐसे बँधे समाज से, महाराज को केवल रथों से नहीं निपटना चाहिए।

panels.shot: wide shot of Vassakara taking his leave from the grove, bowing slightly, monks in the background
panels.action: Vassakara turns to depart the grove, offering a respectful bow, while a line of monks in simple robes moves past behind him in quiet single file.

dialogue.text: The sutta tells that Vassakara left, understanding that as long as the Vajjis kept these habits, their decline would be hard to bring about.

i18n.hi: सुत्त कहता है, वस्सकार लौट गया, समझकर कि जब तक वज्जि ये आदतें निभाएँगे, उनका ढलान लाना कठिन होगा।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide of the plains between Magadha and Vajji, with faint markers for rivers and cities, a sense of looming conflict
panels.action: From high above, the flat expanse of the Ganga plains stretches between Rajagriha and Vaishali, rivers glinting like threads, roads faintly visible, small clusters of huts marking towns along the way.

dialogue.text: Later traditions speak of a long war between Magadha and Vajji, even of sixteen hard years, but historians treat such numbers with caution, hearing in them the echo of memory rather than a record.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा मगध–वज्जि के लम्बे युद्ध की बात करती है, सोलह कठोर सालों तक, पर इतिहासकार ऐसे आँकड़ों को सँभालकर लेते हैं, इनमें रिकॉर्ड से ज़्यादा याद की गूँज सुनते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot of a later monk copying palm-leaf manuscripts in a monastery, suggesting the fixing of the text
panels.action: Centuries later, in a quiet monastery hall, a monk bends over a palm leaf, stylus in hand, copying careful lines as rows of bound leaves lie stacked beside him.

dialogue.text: By around the fourth century BCE, the discourse had taken shape in the canon, preserving not a verbatim court transcript, but a Buddhist memory of what held a republic together.

i18n.hi: चौथी सदी ईसा पूर्व तक, यह चर्चा काणन में ठहर चुकी थी, शाब्दिक दरबारी बयान नहीं, बल्कि गणराज को थामे रखने वाली बौद्ध स्मृति बनकर।

panels.shot: wide shot juxtaposing a modern legislative hall faintly superimposed with the ancient Vajji assembly, time-spanning composition
panels.action: An ancient hall of wooden beams and seated elders dissolves into the outline of a modern legislative chamber, rows of seats and a central floor echoing the old semicircle of the Vajji assembly.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars see in the Vajjis an aristocratic gana-sangha, not a full democracy, yet the seven conditions still speak of how institutions endure when their habits endure.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान वज्जि को कुलीन गण-संघ मानते हैं, पूरा लोकतंत्र नहीं, पर फिर भी ये सात शर्तें दिखाती हैं कि संस्थाएँ तब तक टिकती हैं, जब तक उनकी आदतें टिकती हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Vassakara’s earlier silhouette against the hills, fading into the text-copying monk, suggesting continuity of questions
panels.action: The silhouette of Vassakara once again stands against Rajagriha’s hills, then softly fades into the image of the monk at his manuscript, as if the minister’s question lives on in the lines being etched.

dialogue.text: A Magadhan minister seeking a way to break a rival left behind, through a monk’s memory, a different legacy: a warning that it is the daily habits of a people that decide whether their house stands or falls.

i18n.hi: एक मगधी मंत्री जो प्रतिद्वंद्वी को तोड़ने का तरीका खोज रहा था, उसी ने भिक्षु की याद के ज़रिए और विरासत छोड़ी: चेतावनी कि किसी समाज का घर रोज़ की आदतें तय करती हैं — टिकेगा या ढहेगा।

title_i18n.en: The Seven Conditions Recited at Rajgir

subtitle_i18n.en: How a question of war became a charter of endurance
subtitle_i18n.hi: जंग का सवाल, धीरज का घोषणापत्र
